title: Home renovation sales
tagline: Learn to guide homeowners from storm damage or aging roofs through a trusted renovation plan.
you_are: a residential roofing and renovation consultant
setting: Conversations happen at the homeowner’s kitchen table after an exterior inspection, or by phone when the homeowner requests a callback.

scenarios.label: Storm damage inspection follow-up
scenarios.desc: Follow up on a free inspection after a hail event to show findings and explain insurance coordination.
scenarios.setup: The homeowner watched you climb the ladder. They are at the kitchen table with coffee. They say: I saw you taking pictures up there, what did you find?
scenarios.skills: Inspection storytelling and insurance process clarity
scenarios.objective: Walk the homeowner through the damage report and secure a signed contingency agreement for the insurance claim.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:15 am, late spring light through the window

scenarios.label: Aging roof full replacement consult
scenarios.desc: Guide a homeowner whose 20-year roof is curling and leaking toward a full system replacement.
scenarios.setup: The homeowner invited you in after a phone screening. They sit with a notepad. They say: Three other guys gave me prices, why are you higher?
scenarios.objective: Present the full roof system upgrade and earn a commitment to schedule the install.
scenarios.place: Living room with sample shingles and deck
scenarios.moment: Saturday 9:30 am, dust motes in the air

scenarios.label: Multi-trade renovation scope creep
scenarios.desc: Manage a whole-home exterior project where the homeowner keeps adding siding, gutters and windows.
scenarios.setup: The homeowner texts you mid-project, then meets at the site. They say: While the crew is here, can we just redo the deck and add a skylight?
scenarios.skills: Change order control and budget protection
scenarios.objective: Finalize a signed change order with clear pricing and timeline impact before any new work starts.
scenarios.place: Job site with scaffolding and tarps
scenarios.moment: Thursday 2:00 pm, compressor whine in background

buyers.angle: Wants to understand benefits without feeling pressured.
Prioritizes visible spending and ROI concerns.
Needs proof before committing despite interest.
Challenges price by comparing DIY costs.
Presses timeline but fears hidden costs.

objections: I’m not sure if a new roof will increase my home’s value enough to justify the cost
Roofing seems like a big expense when I have other home projects pending
I’ve heard roofing contractors sometimes overestimate the needed repairs
I’m not convinced the energy savings will offset the installation price
My insurance might cover part of the cost, but I’m not sure how that works
I want to compare multiple bids before deciding on any contractor
I’m concerned about the disruption to my daily routine during the project
I need to check if the materials used are compatible with my existing home style

rubric.label: Inspection storytelling
rubric.what: Translate photos and measurements into a clear narrative the homeowner can repeat to a spouse or adjuster.

rubric.label: Insurance fluency
rubric.what: Explain RCV versus ACV, supplement process, and contingency language without promising coverage.

rubric.label: System value pitch
rubric.what: Contrast a full roof system with a shingle-only quote using ventilation, warranty and labor facts.

rubric.label: Change order discipline
rubric.what: Capture every scope addition in a written change order with price, schedule impact and homeowner signature.

rubric.label: Lien waiver compliance
rubric.what: Provide conditional and final lien waivers at each draw and never ask for payment before the waiver is ready.

rubric.label: Honest ROI framing
rubric.what: Cite realtor data on resale value without guaranteeing dollar-for-dollar return or tax benefits.

pitfalls: Promising the insurance company will approve the full supplement before the adjuster reinspects.
Collecting a progress payment without delivering a signed conditional lien waiver.
Guaranteeing a specific percentage return on investment at resale.
line: Selling roofing and home renovations to homeowners

research.text: The sources indicate that roofing and home renovations are common upgrades, with roofing being the most common exterior renovation in the first quarter of 2024, accounting for 22% of renovations at an average cost of $12,000. Homeowners spent $463 billion on home renovations in the first quarter of 2024, with roofing recommended by 33% of Realtors as a beneficial upgrade before selling a home. However, while a new roof improves comfort and can be financially beneficial, it does not guarantee a full return on investment when selling a home. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on customer objections or specific conversation details regarding selling roofing and home renovations to homeowners.
